newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police hunt serial killer.
newsitem.headline: Australian police hunt serial killer.

text.p: Australian police said on Friday they were hunting a serial killer preying on young women at nightclubs in the western city of Perth after the discovery of the corpse of a missing woman.
Three young women, all similar in looks and who all attended the same exclusive school, have gone missing from nightclubs in the upmarket Perth suburb of Claremont in the past 14 months.
Two have been murdered and police believe the other, whose body has not been found, was also murdered by a serial killer.
"We are looking at the same offender, a serial offender for the three offences. However, he may have an accomplice," police superintendent Paul Ferguson said on Friday.
Lawyer Ciara Glennon, 27, was discovered in a bush grave in a northern Perth suburb on Thursday after she disappeared on March 14 after leaving a nightclub.

"As terrible as this discovery is, it is a major breakthrough for the investigators of the taskforce," Ferguson said. "The discovery of the body will have a significant impact on the person responsible and will result in him being preoccupied and distracted," Ferguson said.
Jane Rimmer's naked and decomposed body was found face-down in swampy shrubland in a southern Perth suburb in August 1996, two months after she went missing from a Claremont nightclub.
Police have not said how the women were killed.
Legal secretary Sarah Spiers, 18, disappeared in January 1996 after visiting another Claremont nightclub. Police presumed she was murdered, although her body has not been recovered.

Using a psychological profile of the killer, police on Friday appealed to Perth employers to report any unusual activity by workers, such as absenteeism, reclusiveness, headaches, anxiety or inability to concentrate.
"These signs will be noticable to those in contact with the person responsible," Ferguson said.
"Serial offenders of this nature have been found to be compulsive drivers who spend a lot of time in their vehicle and are concerned with the appearance of their car," he said.
"It is likely the individual responsible for these disappearances spent time cleaning or polishing the vehicle he used following the disappearances..."
A police taskforce was established after Rimmer, a 23-year-old child care worker, vanished after leaving a nightclub about midnight on June 9, 1996.
All three women were blondes with a striking similarity in appeaance. All went to the same prestigous Perth school, Iona Presentation College.
Police have offered a A$250,000 (US$195,000) reward for information about the women's disappearance and murders.
Australia's most notorious serial killer, Ivan Milat, received a life sentence last year for the murder of seven backpackers, including five Europeans, outside Sydney.
